metadata.note: The Waynesburg and Washington Railroad ('the Waynie'), a 28.2 mi 3 ft gauge steam line between the Greene and Washington county seats, Waynesburg - Washington, PA, passenger service Oct 31 1877 - Jul 9 1929. One feature, no branches. Research report: research/branches/waynesburg_and_washington_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-22).
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952) -- Table 175 'WAYNESBURG AND WASHINGTON R.R.', 'Freight Service only' (lines 69939-69946)
Chronicling America (loc.gov): Wheeling Daily Intelligencer 1877-03-30 p1, 1878-10-05 p1; Wheeling Daily Register 1877-10-24 p1, 1878-01-15 p2, 1878-04-09 p2
metadata.operator_split: None. The PRR bought stock control in 1885 (Wikipedia, GCHS) or 1888 (Bridgeville Hist. Soc.); the W&W kept running its trains as a named company ('It operated as the W&W until 1920', BHS) and was never merged: the Feb 1952 Official Guide still prints 'WAYNESBURG & WASHINGTON RAILROAD COMPANY' in the PRR header and titles Table 175 'WAYNESBURG AND WASHINGTON R.R.', and the 1929 UP wire story calls it the 'Waynesburg & Washington narrow gauge railroad'. The candidate split date, 1920 (equipment relettered PENNSYLVANIA, GCHS; made part of the Panhandle division, Observer-Reporter, undated), rests on relettering, not on a lease or operating agreement, so the feature is not split. See not_yet_sourced.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn (Rule 1). Excluded: everything after the last passenger run of Jul 9 1929 - W&W steam freight to Apr 6 1933, then a Ford/Kalamazoo railtruck; the north end (Washington - Hackney) standard-gauged in the 1940s for coal; 'Freight Service only' in Feb 1952 Guide Table 175; Penn Central 1968, Conrail 1976; rails scrapped 1978. Also not drawn: the Waynesburg Southern (1966+, freight only) and the Monongahela Railway at Waynesburg (daggered freight-only in 1952), neither a W&W predecessor.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Nothing removed: steam from opening (locomotive No. 2 delivered Sept 1877).
metadata.omitted: No W&W passenger branches exist. The PRR/Panhandle Chartiers branch (Carnegie - Washington), which the W&W met at Washington, is a separate PRR line not covered by this report and is not drawn here; its OSM ways (old_railway_operator=PRR, note:old_railway_operator=Panhandle) start about 300 m north of the W&W's mapped end and were kept out of the trace.
not_yet_sourced: Operator 1920-1929: GCHS says the W&W 'lost its identity' in 1920 when the PRR relettered all equipment 'PENNSYLVANIA', and the Observer-Reporter says the PRR made it part of its Panhandle division (undated). If a PRR annual report, the ICC valuation report for the W&W, or a 1920s Official Guide shows the PRR running the trains in its own name from 1920, the feature should be split at 1920 into W&W 1877-1920 and Pennsylvania Railroad 1920-1929 (PRR colour, pulled programmatically). Until then, one W&W feature.
PRR control date: 1885 (Wikipedia, GCHS) vs 1888 (Bridgeville Hist. Soc.). Not material to the drawn years.

Opening: Oct 31 1877 rests only on the Observer-Reporter (2013, secondary). Primary Wheeling papers show construction still under way on Oct 24 1877, the line completed to Washington by Jan 15 1878, and passenger receipts in Feb 1878 for a road 'not yet fully opened'. 1878 is the first primary-confirmed year; partial working before completion (e.g. Washington - Hackney) is possible but undocumented.

End: one unsourced forum post says passenger service ended in 1931; contradicted by the contemporary 1929 UP story and every local history. No 1930-33 timetable was seen; a mixed train carrying passengers after Jul 1929, if ever sourced, would extend the line.

Wikipedia's PRR-predecessor list says the W&W 'was dissolved October 7, 1932', conflicting with the Feb 1952 Guide listing the company and Wikipedia's PA railroads list (W&W 1875-1976). Recorded, not resolved; does not affect passenger years.

headway_min (150) and avg_speed_kmh (22) are estimates: the only frequency is John O'Hara's undated, unsourced 'six passenger trains in and a like number back' (via marcavitch.com), and no running time was found.

Washington terminal: the W&W depot site, and whether the W&W ran into the PRR (Chartiers branch) station before or after the turn-of-the-century connection (marcavitch.com), are not established; the line is drawn to the end of the OSM W&W grade near W. Beau Street.

properties.speed_source: estimate, not sourced: no W&W running time was found for any year; a figure typical of a 3 ft gauge steam line with 174 curves (Observer-Reporter) and frequent stops
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror): ways tagged old_railway_operator='Waynesburg and Washington' (1252857048, 683031884, 1427674254, 1427674253, 1427674255, 1427674256, 1427674257, 1427674258), routed with opstrace.py (note:old_railway_operator counted as an operator key), Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals; Washington-end pieces stitched in order. OpenHistoricalMap queried for the corridor: no ways.
properties.geometry_quality: Waynesburg - Washington: 28.44 mi drawn against 28.2 mi documented (Fowler s.471, 1919 timetable; Feb 1952 Guide Table 175), +0.9 %. Real-traced with opstrace.py on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator='Waynesburg and Washington': 27.2 mi on ways 1252857048 (Waynesburg - Rees Mill, 3.05 mi) and 683031884 (Rees Mill - south edge of Washington, 24.2 mi), both railway=abandoned mapped from USGS topo, no other operator's track used. The Washington end is stitched in order from the short W&W-tagged ways 1427674254, 1427674253, 1427674255, 1427674256 (abandoned grade) and 1427674257, 1427674258 (now service lanes); the gaps between them are short straight joins of 94, 114, 258 and 153 m (0.38 mi together). APPROXIMATED (straight line): one leg, downtown Washington between W&W ways 1427674256 (at Jefferson Ave / B&O crossing) and 1427674257 (Mill St / W. Beau St), 0.38 mi (608 m): no surviving way follows the grade through the built-up blocks. Total straight-line drawing about 0.76 mi including the short joins. Waypoint fit: West Waynesburg 0.2 km, Rees Mill 0.0, West Union 0.0, Hackney 0.1, West Amity 0.1, Baker 0.0, Vankirk 0.1, Braddock 0.0. Termini: Waynesburg end is the south end of OSM way 1252857048 (39.8920, -80.1902), in Waynesburg borough about 0.6 km SW of the centre; Washington end is the north end of OSM way 1427674258 (40.1701, -80.2526, near W. Beau / Washington St), about 300 m short of where the OSM PRR/Panhandle Chartiers grade (old_railway_operator=PRR, note:old_railway_operator=Panhandle) begins - the exact W&W depot site and whether the W&W ran into the PRR station are not established (report UNRESOLVED 6). The PRR/Panhandle ways north of that point are the Chartiers branch, not the W&W, and were not used; nor were the B&O W&P Subdivision, Tylerdale Connecting, Pittsburgh Railways (Jefferson Ave) or Monongahela / Waynesburg Southern ways. OpenHistoricalMap has no way in the corridor (gap fetch returned 0). ERA: the OSM grade is the abandoned line as last mapped on USGS topo sheets, i.e. its final alignment; the north end was standard-gauged in the 1940s after passenger service ended, and any realignment then (or earlier) was not checked, so the drawn line may differ locally from the 1877-1929 narrow-gauge alignment.

segments.note: Waynesburg and Washington Railroad ('the Waynie'), 3 ft gauge, steam throughout: Waynesburg - West Waynesburg - Rees Mill - West Union - Hackney - West Amity - Baker - Vankirk - Summit - Braddock - Washington (connection with the PRR/Panhandle Chartiers line), 28.2 mi (Fowler s.471 from the 1919 timetable; Feb 1952 Guide Table 175 also 28.2). START 1877: first passenger service between the two county seats on Oct 31 1877 (Observer-Reporter 2013, secondary). Contemporary Wheeling papers (Chronicling America) bracket it: iron laid to within two miles of Waynesburg on Oct 24 1877, 'now completed to Washington, a distance of 28 miles' on Jan 15 1878, and passenger receipts in Feb 1878 for a road 'not yet fully opened'; 1878 is the first year confirmed by a primary source (see metadata.not_yet_sourced). May 18 1875 is the charter/'inception' date, not service. END 1929: last passenger run the night of Tuesday July 9 1929 - United Press wire story in the Indianapolis Times, Jul 10 1929 p3, and South Bend News-Times, Jul 12 1929 p28 (conductor James L. Shull died minutes after the last official run; an unscheduled Kiwanis/American Legion special also ran); agrees with the Pittsburgh Press notice of Jul 7 1929 (via Wikipedia), the Greene County Historical Society and the Observer-Reporter. OPERATOR: the PRR bought control in 1885 (Wikipedia, GCHS) or 1888 (Bridgeville Hist. Soc.) - sources conflict - but the W&W kept running as a named company (still titled in the Feb 1952 Guide and in the 1929 wire story); GCHS says the PRR relettered all equipment 'PENNSYLVANIA' in 1920. Not split - see metadata.operator_split. headway_min 150 is an ESTIMATE from John O'Hara's undated, unsourced recollection of 'six passenger trains in and a like number back' (quoted by marcavitch.com), not a timetable figure. After 1929 (not drawn, Rule 1): steam freight to Apr 6 1933, then a railtruck; Washington - Hackney standard-gauged in the 1940s for coal; 'Freight Service only' in the Feb 1952 Guide; Penn Central 1968, Conrail 1976; rails scrapped 1978.
sources: Segment-level: opening Oct 31 1877 from the Observer-Reporter (2013), bracketed by Wheeling Daily Register 1877-10-24 p1 and 1878-01-15 p2 and 1878-04-09 p2 and Wheeling Daily Intelligencer 1878-10-05 p1 (Chronicling America); last passenger run Jul 9 1929 from the United Press wire story (Indianapolis Times 1929-07-10 p3, South Bend News-Times 1929-07-12 p28), agreeing with Wikipedia (citing Pittsburgh Press 1929-07-07, not opened) and GCHS; in the public timetable 1893 and 1919 per Fowler s.471. headway_min is NOT SOURCED (estimate from an undated, unsourced recollection).
